diagnosis.root_cause: Customer ONU 4C:D7:C8:51:F8:2F is currently offline and deregistered (MPCP DEREG/Unauth). The OLT, PON port, router, VLAN, RADIUS record, and recent subscriber sessions are healthy, while the ONU had stable normal optical readings before the outage. This points to a customer-side ONU power, cabling, or local fibre issue rather than an OLT, PON-port, or upstream service failure.
evidence: The target ONU is offline in stored state and live probe: online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, exchange=MPCP DEREG, with no current optical readings.
The zero/null RX and TX values are correctly interpreted as no reading caused by the ONU being offline, not as strong optical power.

The seven-day telemetry shows stable normal RX around -22.4 to -23.1 dBm, TX around +2.3 dBm, stable distance of 294 m, healthy bias current, and stable voltage until the recent outage; there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
Other ONUs on EPON0/6 remain online with normal RX/TX readings, ruling against a complete PON-port failure.
The OLT responds normally, all eight PONs tested healthy, and CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are normal; this rules against an OLT failure or health false critical.
The router heartbeat is healthy and its resource usage is normal, ruling against router unreachability.
The customer VLAN is present and matches the expected VLAN 1016, and RADIUS data is present and CRM-consistent, ruling against provisioning, VLAN, and authentication database faults.
The subscriber had normal session frequency and duration, with one session in the last 24 hours and no authentication flapping.
The OLT-wide offline count is 25 of 298, close enough to the network baseline to avoid treating the mass-offline trigger alone as an outage; the excess should be monitored separately.

remediation.action: Contact the customer and verify ONU power, LEDs, power adapter, Ethernet/fibre patching, and the optical termination. Reboot or replace the ONU/power supply if necessary, then verify registration and optical readings. Do not restart or replace the OLT/PON port. Monitor the mass-offline alert because the OLT has 25 offline ONUs versus approximately 14 expected from baseline, but current evidence does not establish a shared PON fault.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
